subject: Learning Methods
title: Study Groups That Actually Work
description: A 60-second lesson on Study Groups That Actually Work.

hook.text: Most study groups fail because they become social hours. The few that succeed follow a structured approach.

buildup.text: Effective groups assign roles: one person teaches a section, others ask questions and find errors in the explanation.

discovery.text: The questioning role is critical. It forces the teacher to defend and refine their understanding under challenge.

twist.text: Groups of three work best. Larger groups diffuse responsibility. Pairs lack the challenge of a dissenting third voice.

climax.text: Form a trio. Rotate who teaches. The other two challenge every claim. This structure transforms social time.

punchline.text: Three people. Rotate the teacher. Challenge everything.

quiz.question: Why do groups of three work best for study sessions?
options: Three is the maximum number of people who can meet easily
A third voice provides challenge that pairs lack without diffusing responsibility
Three allows voting on correct answers
